solutions.latex:
The area under the curve is $A = \dfrac{1}{2}bh = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 4\times 0.5 = 1\ \text{unit}^2$.

So $\displaystyle\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx = 1$ and $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,dx = 0$ for all other values outside of $(0, 4)$, so $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1$. So it could be a continuous probability density function.

If $0 \le x < 2$: $m = \dfrac{0.5}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $y$-intercept $= 0$, so $y = \dfrac{x}{4}$.

If $2 \le x \le 4$: $m = \dfrac{-0.5}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$. When $x = 4$, $y = 0$: $y - 0 = -\dfrac{1}{4}(x - 4)$, so $y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}$.

The probability density function is defined by:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{4} & 0 \le x < 2 \\ 1 - \dfrac{x}{4} & 2 \le x \le 4 \\ 0 & \text{for all other values of } x \end{cases}$$

When the particle stops or turns, $v = 0$: $1 - 2\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{3} = 0$, so $\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\dfrac{\pi t}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}, \dfrac{7\pi}{3}$, so $t = 1, 5, 7$ seconds.

In the first 4 seconds the particle changes direction at $t = 1$, so calculate $t = 0$ to $t = 1$ and $t = 1$ to $t = 4$ separately.

$d = \left|\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(1 - 2\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right)dt\right| + \left|\displaystyle\int_1^4\left(1 - 2\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right)dt\right|$

$= \left|\left[t - \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right]_0^1\right| + \left|\left[t - \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right]_1^4\right|$

$= \left|1 - \dfrac{6}{\pi}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right| + \left|\left(4 + \dfrac{6}{\pi}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - \left(1 - \dfrac{6}{\pi}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right|$

$= \left|1 - \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi}\right| + \left|4 + \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi} - 1 + \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi}\right| = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi} - 1 + 4 + \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi} - 1 + \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi} = 2 + \dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{\pi}$

The exact distance is $\left(2 + \dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{\pi}\right)$ m.

$f(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}x^4 - 2x^2 + 1$, $f'(x) = x^3 - 4x$, $f''(x) = 3x^2 - 4$.

Stationary points at $f'(x) = 0$: $x^3 - 4x = 0$, $x(x^2 - 4) = 0$, $x(x + 2)(x - 2) = 0$, so $x = 0, 2, -2$.

When $x = 0$, $f(x) = 1$; when $x = 2$, $f(x) = -3$; when $x = -2$, $f(x) = -3$.

Classifying: $(0, 1)$: $f''(0) = -4 < 0$, so a maximum point. $(-2, -3)$: $f''(-2) = 8 > 0$, so a minimum point. $(2, -3)$: $f''(2) = 8 > 0$, so a minimum point.

Inflections when $f''(x) = 0$: $3x^2 - 4 = 0$, $x^2 = \dfrac{4}{3}$, $x = \dfrac{\pm 2}{\sqrt{3}}$.

When $x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, $f(x) = -\dfrac{11}{9}$; when $x = \dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{3}}$, $f(x) = -\dfrac{11}{9}$.

Concavity changes: $f''(x) > 0$ for $-2 < x < -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, $f''(x) = 0$ at $x = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, $f''(x) < 0$ for $-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} < x < 0$; the pattern is reversed for $0 < x < 2$.

$f(x)$ is concave down between the two inflection points: $-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} < x < \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.
